tagline: Up the Passumpsic and along a lake that freezes late.
intro: US 5 leaves St. Johnsbury, the county seat where the platform scale was invented in 1830, and follows the Passumpsic River north into Lyndon. At West Burke the byway takes VT 5A, the more direct and easterly of the two roads to Derby, and runs up the east shore of Lake Willoughby beneath Mount Pisgah, with Mount Hor across the water.

The lake is over 300 feet deep in places, and because of that depth it freezes later than the other lakes in the Kingdom. From Derby the road comes down to Newport at the south end of Lake Memphremagog, 51 miles from where it began.

moments.title: Lyndon
moments.text: A town of covered bridges over the branches of the Passumpsic, the Randall from 1865 and the Sanborn from 1867 among them, the Sanborn standing between Lyndon and St. Johnsbury.

moments.title: Devil's Rock, Lake Willoughby
moments.text: A pull-off on the Mount Pisgah shore, where the rock carries a painted devil and, in still water, its reflection is said to show a skull lying on its side.

moments.title: Newport
moments.text: First called Pickeral Point, then Lake Bridge, the city wraps the south shore of Lake Memphremagog, where the Clyde, Barton and Black rivers all come in.
